title: Cerberus rule pack
description: The SHAPE of a rule pack. A pack is a parameterisation of a CLOSED registry of named detector types — Suricata/Sigma shape, not eBPF shape — and this schema describes the parameterisation without carrying any deployment's values. There is deliberately no example threshold, token list, allowlist or honeypot prefix anywhere in this file: a numeric bar's evasion cost is a parameter change, one-time and zero-marginal, so publishing one is pure loss. A pack conforming to this schema is expected to live in a private repository.

version.description: The pack version. Stamped on every ledger row as a CONTENT HASH by the loader, not taken on trust from this field: a pack whose recorded version does not identify its contents makes every historical verdict unreproducible.

secret.description: Values excluded from every dump, log line and error message. Per-site allowlists, honeypot prefixes and any other value whose disclosure is a bypass live here. The loader must be able to render a whole pack for debugging WITHOUT this section — a redaction that has to be remembered at each call site is a redaction that will be forgotten at one of them.

type.description: A value from the engine's CLOSED registry of detector types. A pack cannot define a new detector type — that would be a DSL, and a general expression language over event fields makes writing another 'this key did N of X in window W' counter the easiest thing in the system, which is the exact shape this design exists to remove.

class.description: Enforcement mode, never a weight. `circumstance` may inform a finding and may NEVER convict at any multiplicity.

family.description: The independence key. Two items sharing a family are ONE item; without it, three restatements of a single observation look exactly like three corroborating detectors.

independence_group.description: Collapses families that are not independent OF EACH OTHER — two rules reading the same underlying distribution share a group even though their names differ, and a quorum must count them once.

evasion_class.description: What it costs an adversary to evade this detector, ONCE they know it exists. A detector whose class is `parameter_change` may not enter a public registry and does not count toward forward recall: publishing it hands over the value and buys nothing. This field is what makes that rule checkable rather than a convention.

mode.description: A new detector starts in `shadow`. `enforce` records a verdict AND acts on it.

corroborator.description: A corroborator supplies a SECOND independent family and may never convict alone. It must state its unit explicitly rather than inheriting the unit of whatever rule it is paired with — a corroborator's floors do not change meaning because the rule beside it counts something else.

emission_baseline.description: For any detector reasoning about the ABSENCE of a telemetry field: the rate at which the relevant platforms emit that field at all. Absence is not behaviour until you know the emission rate, and a detector without this may not reason about absence.

source.description: How the baseline was measured, so a stale one is legible as stale.

params.description: The detector's numeric parameters. Values are a property of a DEPLOYMENT and are never published; this schema constrains only that they exist and are numbers.

scan.description: A ScanSpec: the closed, declarative grammar a detector uses to ask for evidence. Every enum here is closed, so a typo is a load error rather than a silently-empty scan.

verdict_filter.description: Every shipped rule uses `none`. A re-derivation that cannot see the rows it convicted revokes its own verdict the moment it runs.

unit.description: 🔴 LOAD-BEARING. Counting events where the rule means sessions pseudo-replicates a real visitor's engagement across many rows and drives a concentration statistic toward a conviction. That is a different rule, and it has shipped as a bug.

group_by.description: There is deliberately no key producing a (fingerprint, site) tuple. Cross-tenant reasoning may produce a COUNT; it must never produce a membership list.

require_fields.description: Declaring an input lets the harness refuse to run outside the window in which that field is trustworthy, rather than returning a confident zero. `timezone_resolvable` is fail-closed: rows whose declared zone does not resolve are DROPPED, never fatal.
